newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished a tad lower on Thursday in thin trade with moderate shortcovering for prompt shipments of RSS3 rubber failing to prop up the market, dealers said.
"It was dull and quiet. The buying thinned out despite further shortcovering for RSS3 rubber which was not enough to lift the local market," a local rubber trader said.

The volume for the February RSS3 rubber contract reached about 1,400 tonnes, down slightly from the previous day's 1,730 tonnes, traders said. Volume in the March RSS3 rubber contract reached 840 tonnes.
Dealers said the volume in the market will remain sparse in the coming days because of weak demand.
"The volume is so bad it's no longer funny. It's been horrible," one trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 122.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.00 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 179.00-181.00 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.29) a kg from the previous 179.50 cents.
February TSR20 was seen at 167.00-169.00 Singapore cents (US$1.19-$1.20) a kg from the previous 169.00 cents.
